source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
So, factory tested all 3 boards: 1 has L3 steady at 3.3V (works), 2 fluctuate 0.5–2V. So the design is fine, looks like an AXP2101 thermal-pad soldering issue on those 2.

The factory is fully automated (stencil + reflow oven, no hand soldering). I checked the gerbers: 13 GND vias under the pad (tented) look fine, but the AXP2101 thermal pad paste is one single full opening. Could that be that there is too much paste, so the chip floats in the reflow oven and grounds inconsistently? Would switching that pad to a segmented "windowpane" paste aperture help the yield?
What do you think?

execution.observed_behavior: Factory testing found that two of three boards had unstable L3 output, and the client identified a suspected AXP2101 thermal-pad soldering and production-yield problem associated with the single full paste opening.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Hi Dusko, they didnt bake AXP before reflow so steam bubbles destroyed 2 AXPs, they said they will bake in full production and replaced 2 AXP in samples, they will send them soon, so lets see when they are here. Thanks for the support.

value_updates.pre_reflow_moisture_control: Bake AXP2101 components before full-production reflow to prevent moisture-related steam damage.
